title: The passive
subtitle: worden + participle, zijn + participle, Er wordt gewerkt

explain.text: In an **active** sentence the doer is the subject: *De bakker bakt het brood.* In a **passive** sentence the thing that is done becomes the subject: *Het brood **wordt** gebakken.* The passive is built with **worden + past participle**, and the participle goes **to the end**. The doer is optional; if you name it, use **door**: *Het brood wordt **door de bakker** gebakken.*

*Worden* changes with the subject: **ik word, jij wordt, hij/zij/het wordt, wij/jullie/zij worden**. After inversion the *t* of *jij wordt* disappears: *Word jij gebeld?* The past is **werd** (singular) and **werden** (plural). Use the passive when **what happens** matters more than **who does it**.

explain.text: **Zijn + participle** describes a **result or state**: *Het pakket **is** bezorgd* (it has been delivered, it is there now). *De winkel **is** gesloten* (the shop is closed). Compare **worden**, which describes the **process**: *Het pakket **wordt** bezorgd* (it is being delivered). So *is bezorgd* is also the **perfect passive**: *Het pakket is gisteren bezorgd.*

Note that Dutch does not say *is bezorgd geworden* in everyday use: the perfect passive is simply **zijn + participle**. The past forms are **was / waren + participle**: *Toen ik aankwam, was de winkel al gesloten.* This also means: *The shop had been closed.* A doer is still possible: *De straat is door de gemeente afgesloten.*

explain.nl: Toen wij aankwamen, was de winkel al gesloten.
explain.en: When we arrived, the shop was already closed.

explain.text: Ask yourself: is it **happening** (worden) or **finished** (zijn)? *De deur wordt gesloten* = someone is closing it. *De deur is gesloten* = it is shut.

lessons.title: Er wordt gewerkt: impersonal passive and modals

explain.text: Dutch can make a passive even from a verb **without an object**, when the doer is people in general or does not matter: *Er wordt hard gewerkt.* (people are working hard.) *Er wordt hier niet gerookt.* There is no real subject, so **er** takes the first position. If another element opens the sentence, you drop it: *Hier wordt niet gerookt.*

With a **modal verb** the passive goes at the end: modal + participle + **worden**: *Het formulier moet ingevuld worden.* The order *moet worden ingevuld* is also correct. In a subordinate clause: *…dat het formulier ingevuld moet worden.* For the doer use **door**, for a tool use **met**: *Het brood wordt **met de hand** gebakken.*
